(i) 2x^4y^-4 / (8x^7y^3) = (2/8) x x^(4-7) x y^(-4-3) = (1/4) x x^-3 x y^-7 = 1/(4x^3y^7).
(ii) x^-4 / y^-8 = (1/x^4) / (1/y^8) = y^8 / x^4.
(iii) 6x^7 / (2x^4) = (6/2) x x^(7-4) = 3x^3.
(iv) (27)^(-2/3): first 27^(1/3) = cube root of 27 = 3. Then (27)^(2/3) = 3^2 = 9, and the negative power gives the reciprocal: (27)^(-2/3) = 1/9.
(v) (32x^10)^(2/5) = 32^(2/5) x x^(10 x 2/5). Now 32^(1/5) = fifth root of 32 = 2, so 32^(2/5) = 2^2 = 4, and x^(20/5) = x^4. Result: 4x^4.
(vi) (81a^4)^(3/2) = 81^(3/2) x a^(4 x 3/2). Now 81^(1/2) = square root of 81 = 9, so 81^(3/2) = 9^3 = 729, and a^6. Result: 729a^6.
(vii) 2x^-2y^2 x 2x^3y = (2 x 2) x x^(-2+3) x y^(2+1) = 4 x x^1 x y^3 = 4xy^3.
(viii) (2^5)^2 = 2^10 and 8^3 = (2^3)^3 = 2^9. So the fraction = 2^10 x 7^3 / (2^9 x 7^-1) = 2^(10-9) x 7^(3-(-1)) = 2 x 7^4 = 2 x 2401 = 4802.
(ix) (3^5 x a^7b^4) / (3^3 x a^5b^2) = 3^(5-3) x a^(7-5) x b^(4-2) = 3^2 x a^2 x b^2 = 9a^2b^2.

mcqs.q: Simplify in exponential form: 2^4 x 5^4
mcqs.why: Both powers have the same exponent 4, so use x^m x y^m = (xy)^m in reverse: 2^4 x 5^4 = (2 x 5)^4 = 10^4.

mcqs.q: Simplify in exponential form: (2^4)^3
mcqs.why: By the power of a power law (x^m)^n = x^(mn), the exponents are multiplied, not added: (2^4)^3 = 2^(4 x 3) = 2^12.

mcqs.q: Simplify in exponential form: 9^8 / 9^3
mcqs.why: By the quotient law x^m / x^n = x^(m - n), subtract the exponents: 9^8 / 9^3 = 9^(8 - 3) = 9^5.

mcqs.q: Simplify in exponential form: t^4 x t^3
mcqs.why: By the product law x^m x x^n = x^(m + n), add the exponents for the same base t: t^4 x t^3 = t^(4 + 3) = t^7.

mcqs.q: Simplify in exponential form: a^4 x a^9
mcqs.why: By the product law x^m x x^n = x^(m + n), add the exponents: a^4 x a^9 = a^(4 + 9) = a^13. The exponents are added, not multiplied.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 5^0 x 3^0
mcqs.why: By the zero power law x^0 = 1 for any non-zero base: 5^0 = 1 and 3^0 = 1, so 5^0 x 3^0 = 1 x 1 = 1.

mcqs.q: Simplify: x^2y^5 / (xy^4)
mcqs.why: Apply the quotient law to each base separately: x^(2 - 1) = x^1 and y^(5 - 4) = y^1, so x^2y^5 / (xy^4) = xy.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 6x^7 / (2x^4)
mcqs.why: Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents: (6 / 2) x x^(7 - 4) = 3 x x^3 = 3x^3, using x^m / x^n = x^(m - n).

mcqs.q: Simplify: (27)^(-2/3)
mcqs.why: First 27^(1/3) = cube root of 27 = 3, so 27^(2/3) = 3^2 = 9. The negative power then gives the reciprocal: (27)^(-2/3) = 1/9.
32^(1/5) = fifth root of 32 = 2, so 32^(2/5) = 2^2 = 4. Also x^(10 x 2/5) = x^4. Together the result is 4x^4.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.16
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Express each number in standard form: (i) 5.18 x 10^7 (ii) 9.203 x 10^-10 (iii) 2.169 x 10^8 (iv) 7.2 x 10^5 (v) 5.4 x 10^-6 (vi) 5.4105 x 10^-12

Standard form here means the ordinary (usual) form of the number: multiply by the power of 10, moving the decimal point right for a positive power and left for a negative power.
(i) 5.18 x 10^7 = 5.18 x 10000000 = 51800000.
(ii) 9.203 x 10^-10 = 9.203 / 10^10 = 0.0000000009203.
(iii) 2.169 x 10^8 = 2.169 x 100000000 = 216900000.
(iv) 7.2 x 10^5 = 7.2 x 100000 = 720000.
(v) 5.4 x 10^-6 = 5.4 / 10^6 = 0.0000054.
(vi) 5.4105 x 10^-12 = 5.4105 / 10^12 = 0.0000000000054105.

Q2. Express each number in scientific notation: (i) 5620000 (ii) 0.0000014 (iii) 874020000 (iv) 7,586,000,000,000,000 (v) 4,460,500,000,000 (vi) 0.0000000000995

Scientific notation is the form a x 10^b where 1 <= a < 10 and b is an integer. Count the places the decimal point moves: moving left gives a positive b, moving right gives a negative b.
(i) 5620000 = 5.62 x 1000000 = 5.62 x 10^6 (point moved 6 places left).
(ii) 0.0000014 = 1.4 / 1000000 = 1.4 x 10^-6 (point moved 6 places right).
(iii) 874020000 = 8.7402 x 100000000 = 8.7402 x 10^8 (point moved 8 places left).
(iv) 7,586,000,000,000,000 = 7.586 x 10^15 (point moved 15 places left).
(v) 4,460,500,000,000 = 4.4605 x 10^12 (point moved 12 places left).
(vi) 0.0000000000995 = 9.95 x 10^-11 (point moved 11 places right).
Note: The printed Answers give (v) as 4.4605 x 10^8. That is wrong: 4,460,500,000,000 has 13 digits, so the decimal point moves 12 places and the correct form is 4.4605 x 10^12.

mcqs.q: Express 5.18 x 10^7 in ordinary (usual) form
mcqs.why: A positive power of 10 moves the decimal point to the right: 5.18 x 10^7 = 5.18 x 10000000 = 51800000, with the point moved 7 places right.

mcqs.q: Express 7.2 x 10^5 in ordinary (usual) form
mcqs.why: Multiply by 10^5 = 100000, moving the decimal point 5 places right: 7.2 x 10^5 = 7.2 x 100000 = 720000.

mcqs.q: Express 5.4 x 10^-6 in ordinary (usual) form
mcqs.why: A negative power means divide: 5.4 x 10^-6 = 5.4 / 10^6, moving the decimal point 6 places left, which gives 0.0000054.

mcqs.q: Express 9.203 x 10^-10 in ordinary (usual) form
mcqs.why: 9.203 x 10^-10 = 9.203 / 10^10, so the decimal point moves 10 places left from 9.203, giving 0.0000000009203.

mcqs.q: Express 2.169 x 10^8 in ordinary (usual) form
mcqs.why: Multiply by 10^8 = 100000000, moving the decimal point 8 places right: 2.169 x 10^8 = 2.169 x 100000000 = 216900000.

mcqs.q: Express 5620000 in scientific notation
mcqs.why: Scientific notation is a x 10^b with 1 <= a < 10. Moving the decimal point 6 places left in 5620000 gives 5.62, so 5620000 = 5.62 x 10^6.

mcqs.q: Express 0.0000014 in scientific notation
mcqs.why: Move the decimal point 6 places right to get 1.4, which is between 1 and 10. Moving right gives a negative power, so 0.0000014 = 1.4 x 10^-6.

mcqs.q: Express 874020000 in scientific notation
mcqs.why: Move the decimal point 8 places left in 874020000 to get 8.7402, which satisfies 1 <= a < 10. So 874020000 = 8.7402 x 10^8.

mcqs.q: Express 4,460,500,000,000 in scientific notation
mcqs.why: The number has 13 digits, so the decimal point moves 12 places left to give 4.4605. Hence 4,460,500,000,000 = 4.4605 x 10^12, not 10^8.

mcqs.q: Express 0.0000000000995 in scientific notation
mcqs.why: Move the decimal point 11 places right to get 9.95, which is between 1 and 10. Moving right gives a negative power, so the number is 9.95 x 10^-11.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.17
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Write each equation in slope-intercept form. Also find the slope and y-intercept: (i) 10x + 35 = -5y (ii) x + 4y = 8 (iii) -8x + y = 5 (iv) 2y - 8 = 6x (v) 3y = 15x + 9 (vi) 3 = x/4 + y

The slope-intercept form is y = mx + c, where m is the slope and the y-intercept is the point (0, c). Make y the subject in each equation.
(i) 10x + 35 = -5y. Divide both sides by -5: y = (10x + 35)/(-5) = -2x - 7. Slope = -2, y-intercept = (0, -7).
(ii) x + 4y = 8. Subtract x: 4y = -x + 8. Divide by 4: y = -(1/4)x + 2. Slope = -1/4, y-intercept = (0, 2).
(iii) -8x + y = 5. Add 8x: y = 8x + 5. Slope = 8, y-intercept = (0, 5).
(iv) 2y - 8 = 6x. Add 8: 2y = 6x + 8. Divide by 2: y = 3x + 4. Slope = 3, y-intercept = (0, 4).
(v) 3y = 15x + 9. Divide by 3: y = 5x + 3. Slope = 5, y-intercept = (0, 3).
(vi) 3 = x/4 + y. Subtract x/4: y = -x/4 + 3. Slope = -1/4, y-intercept = (0, 3).

Q2. If 2x + y = 4, then find the value of y when x = 13

Substitute x = 13 in the equation 2x + y = 4.
2(13) + y = 4, so 26 + y = 4.
y = 4 - 26 = -22.
Hence y = -22. Check: 2(13) + (-22) = 26 - 22 = 4. Correct.

Q3. If 2y - 7x = -3, then find the value of y when x = 3

Substitute x = 3 in the equation 2y - 7x = -3.
2y - 7(3) = -3, so 2y - 21 = -3.
2y = -3 + 21 = 18.
y = 18/2 = 9.
Hence y = 9. Check: 2(9) - 7(3) = 18 - 21 = -3. Correct.

Q4. If 7y - 10x - 70 = 0, then find the value of x when y = -1

Substitute y = -1 in the equation 7y - 10x - 70 = 0.
7(-1) - 10x - 70 = 0, so -7 - 10x - 70 = 0.
-10x - 77 = 0, so -10x = 77.
x = 77/(-10) = -7.7, i.e. x = -77/10.
Check: 7(-1) - 10(-7.7) - 70 = -7 + 77 - 70 = 0. Correct.
Note: The printed Answers give x = -7. That is wrong: putting x = -7 and y = -1 gives 7(-1) - 10(-7) - 70 = -7 + 70 - 70 = -7, which is not 0. The correct value is x = -77/10 = -7.7.

Q5. Make y the subject of each of the following: (i) m - y = s (ii) (y + 3)/2 = x (iii) (x + y)/6 = 2 (iv) y^2 + x = 7 (v) y/2 = 4x - 7 (vi) 10 - 2y = 3x (vii) 2 + 3y = ax + b (viii) x = 2(y + 3)

Rearrange each formula step by step until y is alone on one side.
(i) m - y = s: subtract m: -y = s - m; multiply by -1: y = m - s.
(ii) (y + 3)/2 = x: multiply by 2: y + 3 = 2x; subtract 3: y = 2x - 3.
(iii) (x + y)/6 = 2: multiply by 6: x + y = 12; subtract x: y = 12 - x.
(iv) y^2 + x = 7: subtract x: y^2 = 7 - x; take the square root: y = sqrt(7 - x) (taking the positive value, as in the book).
(v) y/2 = 4x - 7: multiply by 2: y = 2(4x - 7) = 8x - 14.
(vi) 10 - 2y = 3x: subtract 10: -2y = 3x - 10; divide by -2: y = (3x - 10)/(-2) = 5 - 3x/2.
(vii) 2 + 3y = ax + b: subtract 2: 3y = ax + b - 2; divide by 3: y = (ax + b - 2)/3.
(viii) x = 2(y + 3): divide by 2: x/2 = y + 3; subtract 3: y = x/2 - 3.

Q6. If P = a + b + c, make b the subject of the formula and find b when P = 40, a = 10 and c = 7

From P = a + b + c, subtract a and c from both sides: b = P - a - c. So b is now the subject.
Now substitute P = 40, a = 10 and c = 7: b = 40 - 10 - 7.
b = 23.
Check: a + b + c = 10 + 23 + 7 = 40 = P. Correct.

Q7. If A = (h/2)(a + b), make h the subject of the formula. Also find h when a = 4, b = 8 and A = 24

A = (h/2)(a + b). Multiply both sides by 2: 2A = h(a + b).
Divide both sides by (a + b): h = 2A/(a + b). So h is now the subject.
Now substitute A = 24, a = 4 and b = 8: h = 2(24)/(4 + 8) = 48/12 = 4.
Hence h = 4. Check: (h/2)(a + b) = (4/2)(12) = 2 x 12 = 24 = A. Correct.

Q8. If y = (3x - 9)/2, make x the subject. Also find value of x when y = 3

y = (3x - 9)/2. Multiply both sides by 2: 2y = 3x - 9.
Add 9 to both sides: 2y + 9 = 3x.
Divide both sides by 3: x = (2y + 9)/3 = (2/3)y + 3. So x is now the subject.
Now substitute y = 3: x = (2(3) + 9)/3 = (6 + 9)/3 = 15/3 = 5.
Hence x = 5. Check: y = (3(5) - 9)/2 = (15 - 9)/2 = 6/2 = 3. Correct.

Q9. Use the formula y = 100 - 100/(1 + x) to find the value of y when x = 19

Substitute x = 19 in the formula y = 100 - 100/(1 + x).
y = 100 - 100/(1 + 19) = 100 - 100/20.
100/20 = 5, so y = 100 - 5 = 95.
Hence y = 95.

mcqs.q: What is the slope-intercept form of a straight line, and what does m stand for in it?
options: y = mx + c, where m is the slope
y = mx + c, where m is the y-intercept
x = my + c, where m is the slope
y = c/x + m, where m is the slope
mcqs.why: The notes give the slope-intercept form as y = mx + c, where m is the slope and the y-intercept is the point (0, c).

mcqs.q: Write 10x + 35 = -5y in slope-intercept form.
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by -5: y = (10x + 35)/(-5) = -2x - 7. The slope is -2 and the y-intercept is (0, -7).

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line x + 4y = 8?
mcqs.why: Subtract x: 4y = -x + 8. Divide by 4: y = -(1/4)x + 2, so comparing with y = mx + c gives slope m = -1/4.

mcqs.q: What is the y-intercept of the line 2y - 8 = 6x?
mcqs.why: Add 8: 2y = 6x + 8. Divide by 2: y = 3x + 4, so c = 4 and the y-intercept is the point (0, 4).

mcqs.q: If 2x + y = 4, find the value of y when x = 13.
If 2y - 7x = -3, find the value of y when x = 3.
Make y the subject of the formula m - y = s.
mcqs.why: Subtract m from both sides: -y = s - m. Multiply both sides by -1: y = m - s, so y is now alone as the subject.

mcqs.q: Make y the subject of the formula (y + 3)/2 = x.
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by 2: y + 3 = 2x. Subtract 3 from both sides: y = 2x - 3, so y is now the subject of the formula.

mcqs.q: If P = a + b + c, find b when P = 50, a = 12 and c = 9.
mcqs.why: Make b the subject: b = P - a - c. Substitute: b = 50 - 12 - 9 = 29. Check: 12 + 29 + 9 = 50 = P.

mcqs.q: If A = (h/2)(a + b), find h when A = 30, a = 5 and b = 7.
mcqs.why: Make h the subject: h = 2A/(a + b). Substitute: h = 2(30)/(5 + 7) = 60/12 = 5. Check: (5/2)(12) = 30 = A.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.18
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Determine the quadrant of the coordinate plane in which the following points lie: J(3, -7), K(5, 9), L(-4, 4), M(-8, -2)

Use the signs of the coordinates: Quadrant I is (+, +), Quadrant II is (-, +), Quadrant III is (-, -) and Quadrant IV is (+, -).
J(3, -7): x is positive and y is negative, the (+, -) pattern, so J lies in Quadrant IV.
K(5, 9): both coordinates are positive, the (+, +) pattern, so K lies in Quadrant I.
L(-4, 4): x is negative and y is positive, the (-, +) pattern, so L lies in Quadrant II.
M(-8, -2): both coordinates are negative, the (-, -) pattern, so M lies in Quadrant III.

Q2. Draw the graph of each of the following: (i) y = -2 (ii) y = 5 (iii) x = -2 (iv) x = 0 (v) y = 0 (vi) x = 7 (vii) y = -3x (viii) y = (1/2)x (ix) 4x - y = 0 (x) 2x - y = 4 (xi) y = -3x + 3

To draw the graph of a linear equation, find at least two points on the line, plot them and join them with a straight line. Lines of the form y = c are horizontal (parallel to the x-axis) and lines of the form x = a are vertical (parallel to the y-axis).
(i) y = -2: y is -2 for every x. Points: (-1, -2), (0, -2), (1, -2), (2, -2). The graph is the horizontal line 2 units below the x-axis, parallel to the x-axis.
(ii) y = 5: Points: (-1, 5), (0, 5), (1, 5), (2, 5). The graph is the horizontal line 5 units above the x-axis, parallel to the x-axis.
(iii) x = -2: x is -2 for every y. Points: (-2, -1), (-2, 0), (-2, 1), (-2, 2). The graph is the vertical line 2 units to the left of the y-axis, parallel to the y-axis.
(iv) x = 0: Points: (0, -1), (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2). The graph is the y-axis itself.
(v) y = 0: Points: (-1, 0), (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0). The graph is the x-axis itself.
(vi) x = 7: Points: (7, -1), (7, 0), (7, 1), (7, 2). The graph is the vertical line 7 units to the right of the y-axis, parallel to the y-axis.
(vii) y = -3x: Put x = 0: y = 0, point (0, 0). Put x = 1: y = -3, point (1, -3). Put x = -1: y = 3, point (-1, 3). The graph is the straight line through the origin with slope -3.
(viii) y = (1/2)x: Put x = 0: y = 0, point (0, 0). Put x = 2: y = 1, point (2, 1). Put x = -2: y = -1, point (-2, -1). The graph is the straight line through the origin with slope 1/2.
(ix) 4x - y = 0, i.e. y = 4x: Put x = 0: y = 0, point (0, 0). Put x = 1: y = 4, point (1, 4). Put x = -1: y = -4, point (-1, -4). The graph is the straight line through the origin with slope 4.
(x) 2x - y = 4, i.e. y = 2x - 4: Put x = 0: y = -4, point (0, -4). Put x = 2: y = 0, point (2, 0). Put x = 3: y = 2, point (3, 2). The graph is the straight line with slope 2 and y-intercept (0, -4).
(xi) y = -3x + 3: Put x = 0: y = 3, point (0, 3). Put x = 1: y = 0, point (1, 0). Put x = 2: y = -3, point (2, -3). The graph is the straight line with slope -3 and y-intercept (0, 3).

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point J(3, -7) lie?
mcqs.why: J(3, -7) has x positive and y negative, the (+, -) sign pattern, and the notes place the (+, -) pattern in Quadrant IV.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point K(5, 9) lie?
mcqs.why: K(5, 9) has both coordinates positive, the (+, +) sign pattern, and the notes place the (+, +) pattern in Quadrant I.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point L(-4, 4) lie?
mcqs.why: L(-4, 4) has x negative and y positive, the (-, +) sign pattern, and the notes place the (-, +) pattern in Quadrant II.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point M(-8, -2) lie?
mcqs.why: M(-8, -2) has both coordinates negative, the (-, -) sign pattern, and the notes place the (-, -) pattern in Quadrant III.

mcqs.q: Describe the graph of y = 5.
options: A vertical line 5 units to the right of the y-axis
A horizontal line 5 units above the x-axis, parallel to the x-axis
A horizontal line 5 units below the x-axis
mcqs.why: For y = 5, y stays 5 for every x, giving points (-1, 5), (0, 5), (1, 5); lines of the form y = c are horizontal and parallel to the x-axis.

mcqs.q: Describe the graph of x = -2.
options: A horizontal line 2 units below the x-axis
A vertical line 2 units to the right of the y-axis
A vertical line 2 units to the left of the y-axis, parallel to the y-axis
mcqs.why: For x = -2, x stays -2 for every y, giving points (-2, -1), (-2, 0), (-2, 1); lines of the form x = a are vertical and parallel to the y-axis.

mcqs.q: What is the graph of the equation x = 0?
mcqs.why: The points of x = 0 are (0, -1), (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), which all lie on the vertical axis, so the graph is the y-axis itself.

mcqs.q: Which point lies on the graph of y = -3x when x = 1?
mcqs.why: Substitute x = 1 in y = -3x: y = -3(1) = -3, so the point on the line is (1, -3). The line also passes through (0, 0) and (-1, 3).

mcqs.q: What is the y-intercept of the line 2x - y = 4?
mcqs.why: Rewrite as y = 2x - 4. Put x = 0: y = 2(0) - 4 = -4, so the line crosses the y-axis at the point (0, -4), with slope 2.

mcqs.q: Which point lies on the graph of y = -3x + 3 when x = 2?
mcqs.why: Substitute x = 2 in y = -3x + 3: y = -3(2) + 3 = -6 + 3 = -3, so the point on the line is (2, -3).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.19
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Write equations for the following statements: (i) The difference between father's age and daughter's age is 26 years. (ii) The price of 6 biscuits is equal to the price of one chocolate. (iii) If a number is added to three times of another number, the sum is 25. (iv) The division of sum of two numbers by their difference is equal to 1 (2nd number is less than 1st). (v) Twice of any age increased by 7 years becomes y years.

Let the two unknowns be x and y in each statement and translate the words into algebra.
(i) Let father's age = x years and daughter's age = y years. Difference is 26: x - y = 26.
(ii) Let the price of one biscuit = x rupees and the price of one chocolate = y rupees. Price of 6 biscuits = price of one chocolate: 6x = y.
(iii) Let the first number = x and the second number = y. A number added to three times another number gives 25: x + 3y = 25.
(iv) Let the first number = x and the second number = y (y < x). Sum divided by difference equals 1: (x + y)/(x - y) = 1.
(v) Let the age = x years. Twice the age increased by 7 becomes y: 2x + 7 = y.

Q2. Write simultaneous linear equations for the following statements: (i) The sum of two numbers is 10 and their difference is 2. (ii) If double the age of son is added to the age of father, the sum is 54. But if double the age of father is added to the age of son, the sum is 92. (iii) One pen and two erasers cost is Rs. 45 and 2 pens and 3 erasers cost is Rs. 80.

Let the two unknowns be x and y and write one equation for each condition.
(i) Let the numbers be x and y. Sum is 10: x + y = 10. Difference is 2: x - y = 2. Simultaneous equations: x + y = 10 and x - y = 2.
(ii) Let the son's age = x years and the father's age = y years. Double son + father = 54: 2x + y = 54. Double father + son = 92: x + 2y = 92. Simultaneous equations: 2x + y = 54 and x + 2y = 92.
(iii) Let the cost of one pen = Rs. x and the cost of one eraser = Rs. y. One pen and two erasers cost Rs. 45: x + 2y = 45. Two pens and three erasers cost Rs. 80: 2x + 3y = 80. Simultaneous equations: x + 2y = 45 and 2x + 3y = 80.

mcqs.q: The difference between a father's age (x years) and his daughter's age (y years) is 26 years. Which equation shows this?
mcqs.why: Difference means subtraction, and the father is older, so father's age minus daughter's age equals 26: x - y = 26, as set up in the notes.

mcqs.q: If one biscuit costs Rs x and one chocolate costs Rs y, which equation says the price of 6 biscuits equals the price of one chocolate?
mcqs.why: The price of 6 biscuits is 6 times the price of one biscuit, which is 6x, and this equals the price y of one chocolate: 6x = y.

mcqs.q: A number x is added to three times another number y and the sum is 25. Which equation shows this?
mcqs.why: Three times the second number is 3y, and adding the first number x to it gives the sum 25, so the equation is x + 3y = 25.

mcqs.q: The sum of two numbers x and y (y less than x) divided by their difference is equal to 1. Which equation shows this?
mcqs.why: The sum is x + y and the difference is x - y; dividing the sum by the difference and setting it equal to 1 gives (x + y)/(x - y) = 1.

mcqs.q: Twice of an age x, increased by 7 years, becomes y years. Which equation shows this?
mcqs.why: Twice the age is 2x, and increasing that result by 7 gives 2x + 7, which becomes y years, so the equation is 2x + 7 = y.

mcqs.q: Which pair of simultaneous equations shows: the sum of two numbers is 10 and their difference is 2?
mcqs.why: Write one equation for each condition: the sum condition gives x + y = 10 and the difference condition gives x - y = 2, a simultaneous pair.

mcqs.q: Let the son's age be x and the father's age be y. Double the son's age added to the father's age is 54, and double the father's age added to the son's age is 92. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: Double the son is 2x, so 2x + y = 54; double the father is 2y, so x + 2y = 92. Each condition gives one of the simultaneous equations.

mcqs.q: One pen (Rs x) and two erasers (Rs y each) cost Rs 45, and 2 pens and 3 erasers cost Rs 80. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: One pen and two erasers cost x + 2y = 45 rupees; two pens and three erasers cost 2x + 3y = 80 rupees, one equation for each purchase.

mcqs.q: Which pair of simultaneous equations shows: the sum of two numbers is 7 and their difference is 3?
mcqs.why: Following the same translation as the notes: the sum condition gives x + y = 7 and the difference condition gives x - y = 3, one equation per condition.

mcqs.q: Twice of a number x, increased by 5, becomes y. Which equation shows this?
mcqs.why: Twice the number is 2x, and increasing that result by 5 gives 2x + 5, which becomes y, so the equation is 2x + 5 = y.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.20
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Solve the following simultaneous linear equations by the elimination method: (i) 2x + 5y = -1, x - 2y = 4 (ii) x + y = 2, x - y = 0 (iii) 2x + 3y = 3, x + 5y = 5 (iv) x - 4y = 4, 4x - y = 16 (v) 2x - 3y = 6, 3x + 5y = 0 (vi) 3x - 4y = 7, 5x + y = 27

Elimination method: multiply the equations so that the coefficients of one variable become equal, then add or subtract to eliminate that variable; solve for the other variable and put its value back to find the first.
(i) 2x + 5y = -1 ... (a); x - 2y = 4 ... (b). Multiply (b) by 2: 2x - 4y = 8 ... (c). Subtract (c) from (a): (2x + 5y) - (2x - 4y) = -1 - 8, so 9y = -9, y = -1. Put y = -1 in (b): x - 2(-1) = 4, so x + 2 = 4, x = 2. Solution set = {(2, -1)}. Check in (a): 2(2) + 5(-1) = 4 - 5 = -1. Correct.
(ii) x + y = 2 ... (a); x - y = 0 ... (b). Add (a) and (b): 2x = 2, so x = 1. Put x = 1 in (a): 1 + y = 2, so y = 1. Solution set = {(1, 1)}. Check in (b): 1 - 1 = 0. Correct.
(iii) 2x + 3y = 3 ... (a); x + 5y = 5 ... (b). Multiply (b) by 2: 2x + 10y = 10 ... (c). Subtract (a) from (c): 7y = 7, so y = 1. Put y = 1 in (b): x + 5(1) = 5, so x = 0. Solution set = {(0, 1)}. Check in (a): 2(0) + 3(1) = 3. Correct.
(iv) x - 4y = 4 ... (a); 4x - y = 16 ... (b). Multiply (a) by 4: 4x - 16y = 16 ... (c). Subtract (c) from (b): (4x - y) - (4x - 16y) = 16 - 16, so 15y = 0, y = 0. Put y = 0 in (a): x - 0 = 4, so x = 4. Solution set = {(4, 0)}. Check in (b): 4(4) - 0 = 16. Correct.
(v) 2x - 3y = 6 ... (a); 3x + 5y = 0 ... (b). Multiply (a) by 3: 6x - 9y = 18 ... (c). Multiply (b) by 2: 6x + 10y = 0 ... (d). Subtract (c) from (d): 19y = -18, so y = -18/19. Put y = -18/19 in (a): 2x - 3(-18/19) = 6, so 2x + 54/19 = 6, 2x = 6 - 54/19 = (114 - 54)/19 = 60/19, x = 30/19. Solution set = {(30/19, -18/19)}. Check in (b): 3(30/19) + 5(-18/19) = 90/19 - 90/19 = 0. Correct.
(vi) 3x - 4y = 7 ... (a); 5x + y = 27 ... (b). Multiply (b) by 4: 20x + 4y = 108 ... (c). Add (a) and (c): 23x = 115, so x = 5. Put x = 5 in (b): 5(5) + y = 27, so y = 2. Solution set = {(5, 2)}. Check in (a): 3(5) - 4(2) = 15 - 8 = 7. Correct.

Q2. Solve the following simultaneous linear equations by substitution method: (i) 2x + 2y = 5, x - 2y = 3 (ii) 5x + 2y = 15, -2x + y = 4 (iii) 6x + y = 2, x - 4y = 15 (iv) 2x + 7y = 10, 3x + y = 3 (v) 2x - 4y = -10, y - 5x = -5 (vi) x + 8y = 15, 3x - y = 0

Substitution method: express one variable from one equation, substitute it in the other equation, solve, and put the value back to find the second variable.
(i) 2x + 2y = 5 ... (a); x - 2y = 3 ... (b). From (b): x = 3 + 2y. Put in (a): 2(3 + 2y) + 2y = 5, so 6 + 4y + 2y = 5, 6y = -1, y = -1/6. Then x = 3 + 2(-1/6) = 3 - 1/3 = 8/3. Solution set = {(8/3, -1/6)}. Check in (a): 2(8/3) + 2(-1/6) = 16/3 - 1/3 = 15/3 = 5. Correct.
(ii) 5x + 2y = 15 ... (a); -2x + y = 4 ... (b). From (b): y = 4 + 2x. Put in (a): 5x + 2(4 + 2x) = 15, so 5x + 8 + 4x = 15, 9x = 7, x = 7/9. Then y = 4 + 2(7/9) = 4 + 14/9 = (36 + 14)/9 = 50/9. Solution set = {(7/9, 50/9)}. Check in (b): -2(7/9) + 50/9 = -14/9 + 50/9 = 36/9 = 4. Correct.
(iii) 6x + y = 2 ... (a); x - 4y = 15 ... (b). From (a): y = 2 - 6x. Put in (b): x - 4(2 - 6x) = 15, so x - 8 + 24x = 15, 25x = 23, x = 23/25. Then y = 2 - 6(23/25) = 2 - 138/25 = (50 - 138)/25 = -88/25. Solution set = {(23/25, -88/25)}. Check in (b): 23/25 - 4(-88/25) = 23/25 + 352/25 = 375/25 = 15. Correct.
(iv) 2x + 7y = 10 ... (a); 3x + y = 3 ... (b). From (b): y = 3 - 3x. Put in (a): 2x + 7(3 - 3x) = 10, so 2x + 21 - 21x = 10, -19x = -11, x = 11/19. Then y = 3 - 3(11/19) = 3 - 33/19 = (57 - 33)/19 = 24/19. Solution set = {(11/19, 24/19)}. Check in (a): 2(11/19) + 7(24/19) = 22/19 + 168/19 = 190/19 = 10. Correct.
Note: The printed Answers give (iv) as (11/19, -24/19). That is wrong: with y = -24/19, the first equation gives 2(11/19) + 7(-24/19) = (22 - 168)/19 = -146/19, not 10. The correct value is y = +24/19.
(v) 2x - 4y = -10 ... (a); y - 5x = -5 ... (b). From (b): y = 5x - 5. Put in (a): 2x - 4(5x - 5) = -10, so 2x - 20x + 20 = -10, -18x = -30, x = 30/18 = 5/3. Then y = 5(5/3) - 5 = 25/3 - 15/3 = 10/3. Solution set = {(5/3, 10/3)}. Check in (b): 10/3 - 5(5/3) = 10/3 - 25/3 = -15/3 = -5. Correct.
(vi) x + 8y = 15 ... (a); 3x - y = 0 ... (b). From (b): y = 3x. Put in (a): x + 8(3x) = 15, so x + 24x = 15, 25x = 15, x = 15/25 = 3/5. Then y = 3(3/5) = 9/5. Solution set = {(3/5, 9/5)}. Check in (b): 3(3/5) - 9/5 = 9/5 - 9/5 = 0. Correct.

Q3. Solve the following simultaneous linear equations by graphical method: (i) 2x - y = 2, x + y = 4 (ii) 3x - y = 1, 2x + y = 4 (iii) -x + y = 1, x + y = 3 (iv) x - 4y = 3, 2x + 4y = 0

Graphical method: for each equation, make a table of points, draw the two straight lines on the same axes; the coordinates of the point where the lines cross (intersect) give the solution.
(i) 2x - y = 2 gives y = 2x - 2: points (0, -2), (1, 0), (2, 2). x + y = 4 gives y = 4 - x: points (0, 4), (2, 2), (4, 0). The two lines cross at the point (2, 2). Solution set = {(2, 2)}. Check: 2(2) - 2 = 2 and 2 + 2 = 4. Correct.
(ii) 3x - y = 1 gives y = 3x - 1: points (0, -1), (1, 2), (2, 5). 2x + y = 4 gives y = 4 - 2x: points (0, 4), (1, 2), (2, 0). The two lines cross at the point (1, 2). Solution set = {(1, 2)}. Check: 3(1) - 2 = 1 and 2(1) + 2 = 4. Correct.
(iii) -x + y = 1 gives y = x + 1: points (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3). x + y = 3 gives y = 3 - x: points (0, 3), (1, 2), (3, 0). The two lines cross at the point (1, 2). Solution set = {(1, 2)}. Check: -1 + 2 = 1 and 1 + 2 = 3. Correct.
(iv) x - 4y = 3 gives y = (x - 3)/4: points (3, 0), (1, -1/2), (-1, -1). 2x + 4y = 0 gives y = -x/2: points (0, 0), (1, -1/2), (2, -1). The two lines cross at the point (1, -1/2). Solution set = {(1, -1/2)}. Check: 1 - 4(-1/2) = 1 + 2 = 3 and 2(1) + 4(-1/2) = 2 - 2 = 0. Correct.

mcqs.q: Solve by elimination: 2x + 5y = -1 and x - 2y = 4.
mcqs.why: Multiply the second equation by 2: 2x - 4y = 8. Subtract from the first: 9y = -9, so y = -1. Then x - 2(-1) = 4 gives x = 2. Check: 4 - 5 = -1.

mcqs.q: Solve by elimination: x + y = 2 and x - y = 0.
mcqs.why: Add the two equations: (x + y) + (x - y) = 2 + 0, so 2x = 2 and x = 1. Put x = 1 in x + y = 2: y = 1. Check: 1 - 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Solve by elimination: 3x - 4y = 7 and 5x + y = 27.
mcqs.why: Multiply the second equation by 4: 20x + 4y = 108. Add to the first: 23x = 115, so x = 5. Then 5(5) + y = 27 gives y = 2. Check: 15 - 8 = 7.

mcqs.q: Solve by substitution: x + 8y = 15 and 3x - y = 0.
mcqs.why: From 3x - y = 0, y = 3x. Substitute: x + 8(3x) = 15, so 25x = 15 and x = 3/5. Then y = 3(3/5) = 9/5. Check: 9/5 - 9/5 = 0.

mcqs.q: Solve by substitution: 2x + 2y = 5 and x - 2y = 3.
mcqs.why: From the second equation, x = 3 + 2y. Substitute: 2(3 + 2y) + 2y = 5, so 6 + 6y = 5, y = -1/6, and x = 3 + 2(-1/6) = 8/3. Check: 16/3 - 1/3 = 5.

mcqs.q: Solve graphically: 2x - y = 2 and x + y = 4.
mcqs.why: The lines y = 2x - 2 and y = 4 - x cross at one point; at (2, 2): 2(2) - 2 = 2 and 2 + 2 = 4, so both equations hold and the solution is (2, 2).

mcqs.q: Solve graphically: 3x - y = 1 and 2x + y = 4.
mcqs.why: The lines y = 3x - 1 and y = 4 - 2x cross at one point; at (1, 2): 3(1) - 2 = 1 and 2(1) + 2 = 4, so both equations hold and the solution is (1, 2).

mcqs.q: Solve graphically: x - 4y = 3 and 2x + 4y = 0.
mcqs.why: The lines y = (x - 3)/4 and y = -x/2 cross at one point; at (1, -1/2): 1 - 4(-1/2) = 3 and 2(1) + 4(-1/2) = 0, so the solution is (1, -1/2).

mcqs.q: Solve by elimination: x + y = 7 and x - y = 3.
mcqs.why: Add the equations: (x + y) + (x - y) = 7 + 3, so 2x = 10 and x = 5. Put x = 5 in x + y = 7: y = 2. Check: 5 - 2 = 3.

mcqs.q: In the elimination method, what is the first aim before adding or subtracting the equations?
options: Always make x the subject of the first equation
Draw both lines on the same axes
Multiply the equations so the coefficients of one variable become equal
Replace one variable by a guessed number
mcqs.why: The notes define elimination as: multiply the equations so that the coefficients of one variable become equal, then add or subtract to eliminate that variable.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.21
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Ahmad added 5 in twice of a number. Then he subtracted half of that number from the result. If the remaining number is 8, find the actual number

Let the number be x.
Twice the number is 2x. Adding 5 gives 2x + 5.
Subtracting half the number: 2x + 5 - x/2.
This equals 8, so 2x + 5 - x/2 = 8.
Simplify the x terms: 2x - x/2 = 3x/2, so 3x/2 + 5 = 8.
3x/2 = 8 - 5 = 3.
Multiply both sides by 2: 3x = 6, so x = 2.
Hence the number is 2. Check: twice 2 is 4, plus 5 is 9, minus half of 2 (which is 1) gives 8. Correct.

Q2. One half of a number added in 3 is equal to one quarter of that number subtracted from 1 (verify the statement: half of a number plus 3 equals quarter of the number minus 1). Find the number

Let the number be x.
Half of the number is x/2 and one quarter of the number is x/4.
The statement gives the equation: x/2 + 3 = x/4 - 1.
Multiply every term by 4 (the LCM of 2 and 4): 2x + 12 = x - 4.
Subtract x from both sides: x + 12 = -4.
x = -4 - 12 = -16.
Hence the number is -16. Check: half of -16 is -8, and -8 + 3 = -5; quarter of -16 is -4, and -4 - 1 = -5. Both sides are equal. Correct.

Q3. The sum of two numbers is 5 and their difference is 1. Find the numbers

Let the numbers be x and y.
From the sum: x + y = 5 ... (a). From the difference: x - y = 1 ... (b).
Add (a) and (b): 2x = 6, so x = 3.
Put x = 3 in (a): 3 + y = 5, so y = 2.
Hence the numbers are 3 and 2. Check: 3 + 2 = 5 and 3 - 2 = 1. Correct.

Q4. The difference of two numbers is 4. If twice of one number is added to 3 times of another number, the result is 43. Find the numbers

Let the numbers be x and y, with x the larger.
From the difference: x - y = 4 ... (a). From the second condition: 2x + 3y = 43 ... (b).
From (a): x = y + 4. Put this in (b): 2(y + 4) + 3y = 43, so 2y + 8 + 3y = 43.
5y + 8 = 43, so 5y = 35, y = 7.
Then x = 7 + 4 = 11.
Hence the numbers are 11 and 7. Check: 11 - 7 = 4 and 2(11) + 3(7) = 22 + 21 = 43. Correct.

Q5. Samia is seven years older than her sister Amina. How old is Samia and Amina, if one fourth of Samia's age is equal to half of Amina's age?

Let Amina's age be x years. Then Samia's age is (x + 7) years, because Samia is 7 years older.
One fourth of Samia's age = (x + 7)/4. Half of Amina's age = x/2.
The condition gives: (x + 7)/4 = x/2.
Multiply both sides by 4: x + 7 = 2x.
Subtract x from both sides: 7 = x, so x = 7.
Amina is 7 years old and Samia is 7 + 7 = 14 years old.
Check: one fourth of 14 is 3.5 and half of 7 is 3.5. Equal. Correct.

Q6. Five years ago, the age of Ahsan was 7 times the age of his son Shakeel. After three years, the age of Ahsan will be 4 times the age of Shakeel. Find their present ages

Let the present age of Ahsan be x years and the present age of Shakeel be y years.
Five years ago: Ahsan was (x - 5) and Shakeel was (y - 5), and (x - 5) = 7(y - 5). So x - 5 = 7y - 35, giving x - 7y = -30 ... (a).
After three years: Ahsan will be (x + 3) and Shakeel will be (y + 3), and (x + 3) = 4(y + 3). So x + 3 = 4y + 12, giving x - 4y = 9 ... (b).
Subtract (a) from (b): (x - 4y) - (x - 7y) = 9 - (-30), so 3y = 39, y = 13.
Put y = 13 in (b): x - 4(13) = 9, so x = 9 + 52 = 61.
Ahsan is 61 years old and Shakeel is 13 years old.
Check: five years ago they were 56 and 8, and 56 = 7 x 8. After three years they will be 64 and 16, and 64 = 4 x 16. Correct.

Q7. In a fraction, the denominator exceeds the numerator by 5. If 2 is subtracted from both the numerator and the denominator, then the fraction becomes 1/6. Find the fraction

Let the numerator be x. Then the denominator is (x + 5), and the fraction is x/(x + 5).
Subtracting 2 from both: the new fraction is (x - 2)/(x + 5 - 2) = (x - 2)/(x + 3).
This equals 1/6, so (x - 2)/(x + 3) = 1/6.
Cross-multiply: 6(x - 2) = 1(x + 3), so 6x - 12 = x + 3.
6x - x = 3 + 12, so 5x = 15, x = 3.
The denominator is 3 + 5 = 8.
Hence the fraction is 3/8. Check: subtracting 2 from both gives 1/6. Correct.

Q8. Fida bought 3 kg melons and 4 kg mangoes in Rs 470. Anam bought 5 kg melons and 6 kg mangoes in Rs 730. Find the price of melons and mangoes per kg

Let the price of melons be Rs x per kg and the price of mangoes be Rs y per kg.
Fida: 3x + 4y = 470 ... (a). Anam: 5x + 6y = 730 ... (b).
Multiply (a) by 3: 9x + 12y = 1410 ... (c). Multiply (b) by 2: 10x + 12y = 1460 ... (d).
Subtract (c) from (d): x = 1460 - 1410 = 50.
Put x = 50 in (a): 3(50) + 4y = 470, so 150 + 4y = 470, 4y = 320, y = 80.
Hence melons cost Rs 50 per kg and mangoes cost Rs 80 per kg.
Check with Anam: 5(50) + 6(80) = 250 + 480 = 730. Correct.

Q9. The cost of 2 footballs and 10 basketballs is Rs 2300 and the cost of 7 footballs and 5 basketballs is Rs 2650. Find the cost of each football and basketball

Let the cost of one football be Rs x and the cost of one basketball be Rs y.
First statement: 2x + 10y = 2300 ... (a). Second statement: 7x + 5y = 2650 ... (b).
Divide (a) by 2: x + 5y = 1150 ... (c).
Multiply (c) by 7: 7x + 35y = 8050 ... (d). Subtract (b) from (d): 30y = 8050 - 2650 = 5400, so y = 180.
Put y = 180 in (c): x + 5(180) = 1150, so x + 900 = 1150, x = 250.
Hence one football costs Rs 250 and one basketball costs Rs 180.
Check with the second statement: 7(250) + 5(180) = 1750 + 900 = 2650. Correct.

Q10. When 1 is added to numerator and denominator both of a fraction, then it becomes 2/3. When 2 is subtracted from the numerator and denominator both, then it becomes 1/3. Find the fraction

Let the fraction be x/y, with numerator x and denominator y.
Adding 1 to both: (x + 1)/(y + 1) = 2/3. Cross-multiply: 3(x + 1) = 2(y + 1), so 3x + 3 = 2y + 2, giving 3x - 2y = -1 ... (a).
Subtracting 2 from both: (x - 2)/(y - 2) = 1/3. Cross-multiply: 3(x - 2) = 1(y - 2), so 3x - 6 = y - 2, giving 3x - y = 4 ... (b).
Subtract (a) from (b): (3x - y) - (3x - 2y) = 4 - (-1), so y = 5.
Put y = 5 in (b): 3x - 5 = 4, so 3x = 9, x = 3.
Hence the fraction is 3/5. Check: adding 1 to both gives 4/6 = 2/3; subtracting 2 from both gives 1/3. Correct.

Q11. When numerator and denominator of a fraction are both decreased by 1, then fraction becomes 1/2, and when both are decreased by 3, fraction becomes 1/4. Find the fraction

Let the fraction be x/y, with numerator x and denominator y.
Decreasing both by 1: (x - 1)/(y - 1) = 1/2. Cross-multiply: 2(x - 1) = 1(y - 1), so 2x - 2 = y - 1, giving 2x - y = 1 ... (a).
Decreasing both by 3: (x - 3)/(y - 3) = 1/4. Cross-multiply: 4(x - 3) = 1(y - 3), so 4x - 12 = y - 3, giving 4x - y = 9 ... (b).
Subtract (a) from (b): 2x = 8, so x = 4.
Put x = 4 in (a): 2(4) - y = 1, so y = 7.
Hence the fraction is 4/7. Check: decreasing both by 1 gives 3/6 = 1/2; decreasing both by 3 gives 1/4. Correct.

mcqs.q: Ahmad added 5 to twice of a number, then subtracted half of that number from the result and got 8. Find the number.
mcqs.why: Let the number be x: 2x + 5 - x/2 = 8, so 3x/2 + 5 = 8, 3x/2 = 3, 3x = 6, and x = 2. Check: 4 + 5 - 1 = 8.

mcqs.q: Half of a number added to 3 is equal to one quarter of that number subtracted from 1. Find the number.
mcqs.why: Following the verified reading in the notes, the equation is x/2 + 3 = x/4 - 1. Multiply every term by 4: 2x + 12 = x - 4, so x = -4 - 12 = -16. Check: -8 + 3 = -5 and -4 - 1 = -5.

mcqs.q: The sum of two numbers is 5 and their difference is 1. Find the larger number.
mcqs.why: x + y = 5 and x - y = 1. Add: 2x = 6, so x = 3, and then y = 5 - 3 = 2. The larger number is 3. Check: 3 + 2 = 5 and 3 - 2 = 1.

mcqs.q: The difference of two numbers is 4. Twice one number added to 3 times the other gives 43. Find the larger number.
Samia is 7 years older than her sister Amina, and one fourth of Samia's age equals half of Amina's age. How old is Samia?
mcqs.why: Let Amina be x, so Samia is x + 7: (x + 7)/4 = x/2. Multiply by 4: x + 7 = 2x, so x = 7. Samia is 7 + 7 = 14 years. Check: 14/4 = 3.5 = 7/2.

mcqs.q: Five years ago Ahsan's age was 7 times his son Shakeel's age; after three years it will be 4 times. What is Ahsan's present age?
mcqs.why: (x - 5) = 7(y - 5) gives x - 7y = -30, and (x + 3) = 4(y + 3) gives x - 4y = 9. Subtract: 3y = 39, y = 13, and x = 9 + 4(13) = 61 years. Check: 56 = 7 x 8.

mcqs.q: In a fraction the denominator exceeds the numerator by 5. Subtracting 2 from both gives 1/6. Find the fraction.
mcqs.why: Let the fraction be x/(x + 5): (x - 2)/(x + 3) = 1/6. Cross-multiply: 6x - 12 = x + 3, so 5x = 15, x = 3, and the denominator is 3 + 5 = 8, giving 3/8.

mcqs.q: Fida bought 3 kg melons and 4 kg mangoes for Rs 470; Anam bought 5 kg melons and 6 kg mangoes for Rs 730. Find the price of melons per kg.
mcqs.why: 3x + 4y = 470 and 5x + 6y = 730. Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2: 9x + 12y = 1410 and 10x + 12y = 1460. Subtract: x = 50, so melons cost Rs 50 per kg.

mcqs.q: 2 footballs and 10 basketballs cost Rs 2300; 7 footballs and 5 basketballs cost Rs 2650. Find the cost of one football.
mcqs.why: 2x + 10y = 2300 gives x + 5y = 1150. Multiply by 7 and subtract 7x + 5y = 2650: 30y = 5400, y = 180. Then x = 1150 - 5(180) = 250, so one football costs Rs 250.

mcqs.q: When 1 is added to the numerator and denominator of a fraction it becomes 3/4. When 1 is subtracted from both it becomes 1/2. Find the fraction.
mcqs.why: (x + 1)/(y + 1) = 3/4 gives 4x - 3y = -1, and (x - 1)/(y - 1) = 1/2 gives 2x - y = 1, so y = 2x - 1. Substitute: 4x - 3(2x - 1) = -1, so -2x = -4, x = 2, y = 3, giving 2/3. Check: 3/4 and 1/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.22
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Solve the following and find the solution set: (i) x - 3 < 2 (ii) -7x < 49 (iii) 4x >= 16 (iv) 5x + 5 < -15 (v) 3x - 1 > 17 (vi) -x + 3 <= 6

Rules: the same number can be added to or subtracted from both sides of an inequality without changing it; multiplying or dividing both sides by a positive number keeps the sign of the inequality, but multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign.
(i) x - 3 < 2: add 3 to both sides: x < 5. Solution set = {x | x < 5}.
(ii) -7x < 49: divide both sides by -7; since we divide by a negative number, the sign reverses: x > 49/(-7), so x > -7. Solution set = {x | x > -7}.
(iii) 4x >= 16: divide both sides by 4 (positive, sign unchanged): x >= 4. Solution set = {x | x >= 4}.
(iv) 5x + 5 < -15: subtract 5 from both sides: 5x < -20. Divide by 5: x < -4. Solution set = {x | x < -4}.
(v) 3x - 1 > 17: add 1 to both sides: 3x > 18. Divide by 3: x > 6. Solution set = {x | x > 6}.
(vi) -x + 3 <= 6: subtract 3 from both sides: -x <= 3. Multiply both sides by -1; the sign reverses: x >= -3. Solution set = {x | x >= -3}.

Q2. Solve the following and show the result on the number line: (i) 5x > 2x + 6 (ii) 7x + 6 < 5x (iii) -3x < 21 (iv) -9x > -27

Solve each inequality first, then show its solution on a number line. An open circle is used at the end point because the end value itself is not included in a strict inequality.
(i) 5x > 2x + 6: subtract 2x from both sides: 3x > 6. Divide by 3: x > 2. Solution set = {x | x > 2}. Number line: mark an open circle at 2 and draw the thick line with an arrow to the right of 2, covering all numbers greater than 2.
(ii) 7x + 6 < 5x: subtract 5x from both sides: 2x + 6 < 0. Subtract 6: 2x < -6. Divide by 2: x < -3. Solution set = {x | x < -3}. Number line: mark an open circle at -3 and draw the thick line with an arrow to the left of -3, covering all numbers less than -3.
Note: The printed Answers give the solution set of (ii) as {x | x > -3}. That is wrong: solving gives x < -3, and the book's own printed number line for this part also shows an open circle at -3 with the arrow pointing to the left, which means x < -3.
(iii) -3x < 21: divide both sides by -3; since we divide by a negative number, the sign reverses: x > 21/(-3), so x > -7. Solution set = {x | x > -7}. Number line: mark an open circle at -7 and draw the thick line with an arrow to the right of -7.
(iv) -9x > -27: divide both sides by -9; since we divide by a negative number, the sign reverses: x < (-27)/(-9), so x < 3. Solution set = {x | x < 3}. Number line: mark an open circle at 3 and draw the thick line with an arrow to the left of 3, covering all numbers less than 3.
Note: The printed Answers give the solution set of (iv) as {x | x > 3}. That is wrong: dividing by -9 reverses the sign, giving x < 3, and the book's own printed number line for this part also shows an open circle at 3 with the arrow pointing to the left, which means x < 3.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality x - 3 < 2.
mcqs.why: Add 3 to both sides of x - 3 < 2: x < 2 + 3, so x < 5. Adding the same number to both sides does not change the inequality, giving {x | x < 5}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality -7x < 49.
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by -7: x and 49/(-7) = -7, and dividing by a negative number reverses the sign, so x > -7, giving the solution set {x | x > -7}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 4x >= 16.
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by 4, a positive number, so the sign stays the same: x >= 16/4, so x >= 4, giving the solution set {x | x >= 4}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 5x + 5 < -15.
mcqs.why: Subtract 5 from both sides: 5x < -20. Divide both sides by 5: x < -20/5, so x < -4, giving the solution set {x | x < -4}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 3x - 1 > 17.
mcqs.why: Add 1 to both sides: 3x > 18. Divide both sides by 3: x > 18/3, so x > 6, giving the solution set {x | x > 6}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality -x + 3 <= 6.
mcqs.why: Subtract 3 from both sides: -x <= 3. Multiply both sides by -1, which reverses the sign: x >= -3, giving the solution set {x | x >= -3}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 5x > 2x + 6.
mcqs.why: Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x > 6. Divide both sides by 3: x > 6/3, so x > 2, giving the solution set {x | x > 2}, shown with an open circle at 2.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality -9x > -27.
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by -9: (-27)/(-9) = 3, and dividing by a negative number reverses the sign, so x < 3, giving the solution set {x | x < 3}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 2x - 4 < 10.
mcqs.why: Add 4 to both sides: 2x < 14. Divide both sides by 2, a positive number, so the sign stays: x < 14/2, so x < 7, giving {x | x < 7}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality 7x + 6 < 5x.
mcqs.why: Subtract 5x from both sides: 2x + 6 < 0. Subtract 6: 2x < -6. Divide by 2: x < -3, giving {x | x < -3}, shown with an open circle at -3 and the arrow to the left.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. In the right angled triangles (not drawn to scale), measurements (in cm) of two of the sides are indicated in the figures. Find the value of x in each case: (i) base 5cm, altitude 12cm, hypotenuse x (ii) altitude 6cm, hypotenuse 8cm, base x (iii) altitude 5cm, hypotenuse 13cm, base x (iv) base 24cm, altitude 7cm, hypotenuse x (v) hypotenuse 30cm, altitude 18cm, base x (vi) altitude 8cm, base 6cm, hypotenuse x

Pythagoras theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Altitude)², i.e. c² = a² + b².
(i) x² = 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169, so x = √169 = 13cm.
(ii) Here x is a leg, so x² = 8² − 6² = 64 − 36 = 28, so x = √28 = 2√7 cm ≈ 5.29cm.
(iii) x² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so x = √144 = 12cm.
(iv) x² = 24² + 7² = 576 + 49 = 625, so x = √625 = 25cm.
(v) x² = 30² − 18² = 900 − 324 = 576, so x = √576 = 24cm.
(vi) x² = 8² + 6² = 64 + 36 = 100, so x = √100 = 10cm.

Q2. In an isosceles right angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is 98cm². Find the length of the equal sides.

Let each equal side be a cm. The two legs are equal, so by Pythagoras theorem: a² + a² = (hypotenuse)².
2a² = 98.
a² = 98 ÷ 2 = 49.
a = √49 = 7.
So each equal side is 7cm long.

Q3. A ladder 10m long is made to rest against a wall. Its lower end touches the ground at a distance of 6m from the wall. At what height above the ground the upper end of the ladder rests against the wall?

The ladder is the hypotenuse c = 10m, the distance from the wall is the base a = 6m, and the required height is the altitude b.
By Pythagoras theorem: b² = c² − a².
b² = 10² − 6² = 100 − 36 = 64.
b = √64 = 8.
So the upper end of the ladder rests 8m above the ground.

Q4. The shadow of a pole measured from the foot of the pole is 2.8m long. If the distance from the tip of the shadow to the tip of the pole is 10.5m, then find the length of the pole.

The pole, its shadow and the line from the tip of the shadow to the tip of the pole form a right angled triangle with hypotenuse 10.5m and base 2.8m.
By Pythagoras theorem: (length of pole)² = 10.5² − 2.8².
= 110.25 − 7.84 = 102.41.
Length of pole = √102.41 = 10.12m (approx).
So the pole is about 10.12m long.

Q5. If a, b, c are the lengths of the sides of a triangle ABC, then tell which of the following triangles are not right angled triangles. Any of ∠A, ∠B and ∠C may be a right angle. (i) a = 6, b = 5, c = 7 (ii) a = 8, b = 9, c = √145 (iii) a = 12, b = 5, c = 13

A triangle is right angled only if the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
(i) Longest side is 7: 7² = 49. Other sides: 6² + 5² = 36 + 25 = 61. Since 49 ≠ 61, triangle (i) is NOT right angled.
(ii) Longest side is √145: (√145)² = 145. Other sides: 8² + 9² = 64 + 81 = 145. Since 145 = 145, triangle (ii) IS right angled.
(iii) Longest side is 13: 13² = 169. Other sides: 12² + 5² = 144 + 25 = 169. Since 169 = 169, triangle (iii) IS right angled.
So only triangle (i) is not a right angled triangle.

Q6. In a right angled triangle ABC with hypotenuse c and sides a and b, find the unknown length. (i) a = 60cm, c = 61cm, b = ? (ii) a = 5/12 cm, c = 13/12 cm, b = ? (iii) b = 10m, a = 4√5 m, c = ? (iv) b = 5dm, a = 5√7 dm, c = ? (v) c = 10√2 dm, b = 5√3 dm, a = ?

Use c² = a² + b², so b² = c² − a², a² = c² − b² and c² = a² + b² as needed.
(i) b² = 61² − 60² = 3721 − 3600 = 121, so b = √121 = 11cm.
(ii) b² = (13/12)² − (5/12)² = 169/144 − 25/144 = 144/144 = 1, so b = √1 = 1cm.
(iii) c² = (4√5)² + 10² = 16 × 5 + 100 = 80 + 100 = 180, so c = √180 = 6√5 m.
(iv) c² = (5√7)² + 5² = 25 × 7 + 25 = 175 + 25 = 200, so c = √200 = 10√2 dm.
(v) a² = (10√2)² − (5√3)² = 100 × 2 − 25 × 3 = 200 − 75 = 125, so a = √125 = 5√5 dm.

Q7. The front of a house is in the shape of an equilateral triangle with the measure of side 10m. Find the height of the house.

The altitude of an equilateral triangle bisects the base, so it forms a right angled triangle with hypotenuse 10m and base 10 ÷ 2 = 5m.
By Pythagoras theorem: height² = 10² − 5².
height² = 100 − 25 = 75.
Height = √75 = 5√3 m ≈ 8.66m.
So the height of the house is 5√3 m, about 8.66m.
Note: The printed answer gives only √(a² − 25) without putting a = 10; with a = 10 the correct height is √75 = 5√3 m ≈ 8.66m.

mcqs.q: In a right angled triangle the base is 5cm and the altitude is 12cm. Find the hypotenuse.
mcqs.why: By Pythagoras theorem, x^2 = (base)^2 + (altitude)^2 = 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169, so x = sqrt(169) = 13cm.

mcqs.q: In a right angled triangle the altitude is 6cm and the hypotenuse is 8cm. Find the base x.
mcqs.why: Here x is a leg, so x^2 = (hypotenuse)^2 - (altitude)^2 = 8^2 - 6^2 = 64 - 36 = 28, so x = sqrt(28) = 2sqrt(7) cm, about 5.29cm.

mcqs.q: In a right angled triangle the base is 24cm and the altitude is 7cm. Find the hypotenuse.
mcqs.why: By Pythagoras theorem, x^2 = 24^2 + 7^2 = 576 + 49 = 625, so x = sqrt(625) = 25cm, the hypotenuse of the triangle.

mcqs.q: In a right angled triangle the two shorter sides are 9cm and 12cm. Find the hypotenuse.
mcqs.why: By Pythagoras theorem, hypotenuse^2 = 9^2 + 12^2 = 81 + 144 = 225, so the hypotenuse = sqrt(225) = 15cm.

mcqs.q: A ladder 10m long rests against a wall, with its lower end 6m from the wall. At what height does its upper end rest?
mcqs.why: The ladder is the hypotenuse: height^2 = 10^2 - 6^2 = 100 - 36 = 64, so the height = sqrt(64) = 8m above the ground.

mcqs.q: In an isosceles right angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is 98cm^2. Find the length of each equal side.
mcqs.why: Let each equal side be a: a^2 + a^2 = 98, so 2a^2 = 98, a^2 = 98/2 = 49, and a = sqrt(49) = 7cm for each equal side.

mcqs.q: A triangle has sides a = 6, b = 5 and c = 7. Is it a right angled triangle?
options: Yes, because 6 + 5 = 11 is close to 7 squared
Yes, it is right angled at every angle
No, it is not right angled
It cannot be decided from the sides
mcqs.why: The longest side is 7: 7^2 = 49, while 6^2 + 5^2 = 36 + 25 = 61. Since 49 is not equal to 61, the triangle is not right angled.

mcqs.q: In a right angled triangle with hypotenuse c = 61cm and side a = 60cm, find side b.
mcqs.why: Use b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 61^2 - 60^2 = 3721 - 3600 = 121, so b = sqrt(121) = 11cm, the unknown side of the triangle.

mcqs.q: A ladder 13m long rests against a wall, with its foot 5m from the wall. At what height does its top rest?
mcqs.why: The ladder is the hypotenuse: height^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144, so the height = sqrt(144) = 12m above the ground.

mcqs.q: The front of a house is an equilateral triangle of side 10m. Find its height.
mcqs.why: The altitude bisects the base, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 10m and base 5m: height^2 = 10^2 - 5^2 = 100 - 25 = 75, so height = sqrt(75) = 5sqrt(3) m, about 8.66m.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Calculate the length of an arc of a circle if the radius of an arc is 8cm and the central angle is 40°.

Formula (as in the book): Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr, where x is the central angle and r is the radius. Take π ≈ 22/7.
Here x = 40° and r = 8cm.
L = (40° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 8.
L = (1/9) × (352/7) = 352/63.
L ≈ 5.59cm.
So the arc length is about 5.59cm.

Q2. If central angle of the sector of a circle is 36° and r is 15cm, then what will be the arc length?

Formula: Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr. Take π ≈ 22/7.
Here x = 36° and r = 15cm.
L = (36° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 15.
L = (1/10) × (660/7) = 66/7.
L ≈ 9.43cm.
So the arc length is about 9.43cm.

Q3. Saleem marks an arc of length 8cm and measures its central angle as 120° degrees. What is the radius of the arc?

Formula: Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr. Take π ≈ 22/7.
Here L = 8cm and x = 120°.
8 = (120° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × r.
8 = (1/3) × (44/7) × r = (44/21) × r.
r = 8 × 21 ÷ 44 = 168 ÷ 44 = 42/11 ≈ 3.82cm (exactly r = 12/π cm).
So the radius is about 3.8cm.

Q4. Jamal uses a compass to draw an arc of length 11cm and a radius of 7cm. Find the angle of this arc?

Formula: Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr. Take π ≈ 22/7.
Here L = 11cm and r = 7cm.
11 = (x ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 7.
11 = (x ÷ 360°) × 44.
x ÷ 360° = 11 ÷ 44 = 1/4.
x = 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
So the angle of the arc is 90°.
Note: The printed answer shows 900, which is a misprint for 90° (the degree sign was printed as a 0).

Q5. The radius of the circle is 14 units and the arc subtends an angle of 65° at the centre. What is the length of the arc?

Formula: Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr. Take π ≈ 22/7.
Here x = 65° and r = 14 units.
L = (65° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 14.
L = (13/72) × 88 = 1144/72 ≈ 15.89 units.
So the arc length is about 15.88 units.

Q6. Calculate the perimeter of the sector of circle to 1 decimal place as shown in the figure. (Figure: sector of radius 8cm with central angle 115°)

Perimeter of a sector = Arc length + radius + radius = Arc length + 2 × radius (book, Key fact).
Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr with x = 115° and r = 8cm.
L = (115° ÷ 360°) × 2 × 3.1416 × 8 ≈ 16.06cm.
Perimeter = 16.06 + 8 + 8 = 32.06cm.
To 1 decimal place, the perimeter is 32.1cm (the book's answer key gives 32.06cm before rounding).

Q7. Calculate the perimeter of a sector of circle of radius 10cm and central angle is 90° in terms of pi?

Perimeter of a sector = Arc length + 2 × radius.
Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr = (90° ÷ 360°) × 2π × 10.
L = (1/4) × 20π = 5π cm.
Perimeter = 5π + 2 × 10 = 5π + 20 cm.
So in terms of π the perimeter is (5π + 20) cm, i.e. about 35.71cm.
Note: The printed answer 15.71cm is only the arc length 5π ≈ 15.71cm; it omits the two radii (20cm), so the full perimeter is 5π + 20 ≈ 35.71cm.

Q8. If angle is 130° and radius is 28cm then what will be the arc length and sector area of the circle?

Arc length L = (x ÷ 360°) × 2πr and Area of sector = (x ÷ 360°) × πr². Take π ≈ 22/7, x = 130°, r = 28cm.
Arc length L = (130° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 28 = (13/36) × 176 = 2288/36 ≈ 63.56cm.
Sector area = (130° ÷ 360°) × (22/7) × 28² = (13/36) × (22/7) × 784.
Sector area = (13/36) × 2464 = 32032/36 ≈ 889.78cm².
So the arc length is about 63.55cm and the sector area is about 889.77cm².

Q9. Gulshan wants to create a garden in the shape of a sector of the circle of radius 42 feet and having a central angle of 120° degrees. Calculate the area of the grass which is required to cover the garden.

Area of sector = (x ÷ 360°) × πr². Take π ≈ 22/7, x = 120°, r = 42 feet.
Area = (120° ÷ 360°) × (22/7) × 42².
Area = (1/3) × (22/7) × 1764.
Area = (1/3) × 5544 = 1848 feet².
So grass is required for 1848 square feet.

Q10. A sector of a circle with an area of 26π cm² and has a radius 6cm. What is the measure of the central angle?

Area of sector = (x ÷ 360°) × πr².
26π = (x ÷ 360°) × π × 6².
26π = (x ÷ 360°) × 36π.
x ÷ 360° = 26π ÷ 36π = 26/36 = 13/18.
x = 360° × 13/18 = 260°.
So the central angle is 260°.

Q11. If a clock's face measures 14 inches across, how much area is between the minute and hour hands at 5 O'clock? (Approximate pi to 3.14)

The clock face measures 14 inches across, so diameter = 14 inches and radius r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 inches.
Each hour mark is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 5 o'clock the hands are 5 hour marks apart, so the (smaller) angle between them is 5 × 30° = 150°.
Area between the hands = Area of sector = (x ÷ 360°) × πr² with x = 150°, π ≈ 3.14.
Area = (150° ÷ 360°) × 3.14 × 7² = (5/12) × 3.14 × 49.
Area = (5/12) × 153.86 ≈ 64.108 square inches.
So the area between the hands is about 64.11 square inches.

mcqs.q: Which formula gives the length of an arc of a circle with central angle x and radius r?
options: L = (x/360) x 2 x pi x r
L = 2 x pi x r x 360/x
mcqs.why: The notes give arc length as L = (x/360 degrees) x 2(pi)r: the fraction x/360 of the full circumference 2(pi)r, with pi taken as 22/7 in these exercises.

mcqs.q: Find the arc length for radius 8cm and central angle 40 degrees (pi = 22/7).
Find the arc length for radius 15cm and central angle 36 degrees (pi = 22/7).
An arc of length 8cm has a central angle of 120 degrees. Find its radius (pi = 22/7).
An arc of length 11cm is drawn with radius 7cm. Find its central angle (pi = 22/7).
Find the arc length for radius 14 units and central angle 65 degrees (pi = 22/7).
Find the perimeter of a sector of radius 8cm and central angle 115 degrees, to 1 decimal place (pi = 3.1416).
mcqs.why: Arc length = (115/360) x 2 x 3.1416 x 8 = 16.06cm approx. Perimeter = arc + 2 radii = 16.06 + 8 + 8 = 32.06cm, which is 32.1cm to 1 decimal place.

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter of a sector of radius 10cm and central angle 90 degrees, in terms of pi.
mcqs.why: Arc length = (90/360) x 2 x pi x 10 = (1/4) x 20pi = 5pi cm. Perimeter = arc + 2 radii = 5pi + 2(10) = (5pi + 20) cm, about 35.71cm.

mcqs.q: A sector-shaped garden has radius 42 feet and central angle 120 degrees. Find the area to be covered with grass (pi = 22/7).
A sector has area 26pi cm^2 and radius 6cm. Find its central angle.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the total surface area of the following pyramids: (i) square pyramid with base side 5cm and slant height 4cm (ii) rectangular pyramid with base 8cm × 6cm and slant heights 3cm (for the 8cm edges) and 4cm (for the 6cm edges) (iii) square pyramid with base side 6cm and slant height 12cm

Total surface area of a pyramid = Area of base + sum of the areas of the triangular faces, where each face = (1/2) × base × slant height (book).
(i) Base area = 5 × 5 = 25cm². Each of the 4 faces = (1/2) × 5 × 4 = 10cm², so 4 faces = 40cm². Total surface area = 25 + 40 = 65cm².
(ii) Base area = 8 × 6 = 48cm². Two faces on the 8cm edges = 2 × (1/2) × 8 × 3 = 24cm². Two faces on the 6cm edges = 2 × (1/2) × 6 × 4 = 24cm². Total surface area = 48 + 24 + 24 = 96cm².
(iii) Base area = 6 × 6 = 36cm². Each of the 4 faces = (1/2) × 6 × 12 = 36cm², so 4 faces = 144cm². Total surface area = 36 + 144 = 180cm².
Note: For (i) the printed answer is 75cm², which is wrong: with base 5cm and slant height 4cm the correct total is 25 + 4 × 10 = 65cm² (75cm² would need a slant height of 5cm).

Q2. Find the surface area of a square pyramid of slant height 15cm and base length 12cm.

Surface area = Area of base + 4 × (area of one triangular face).
Area of base = 12 × 12 = 144cm².
Area of one face = (1/2) × base × slant height = (1/2) × 12 × 15 = 90cm².
4 faces = 4 × 90 = 360cm².
Total surface area = 144 + 360 = 504cm².

Q3. The height of a square pyramid is 25cm and the base area of a square pyramid is 256cm². Find its volume and surface area.

Side of the square base: side² = 256, so side = √256 = 16cm.
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height = (1/3) × 256 × 25 = 6400/3 = 2133⅓ cm³.
For the surface area, first find the slant height l. Half of the base side = 16 ÷ 2 = 8cm, so by Pythagoras theorem: l² = 25² + 8² = 625 + 64 = 689, so l = √689 ≈ 26.25cm.
Area of one face = (1/2) × 16 × 26.25 ≈ 210cm², so 4 faces ≈ 839.96cm².
Total surface area = 256 + 839.96 ≈ 1095.96cm².
So the volume is 2133⅓ cm³ and the surface area is about 1095.96cm².

Q4. Find the surface area of a square pyramid with a base length of 5cm and a slant height of 10cm.

Surface area = Area of base + 4 × (area of one face).
Area of base = 5 × 5 = 25cm².
Area of one face = (1/2) × 5 × 10 = 25cm², so 4 faces = 100cm².
Total surface area = 25 + 100 = 125cm².

Q5. Find the total surface area of the square based pyramid shown in Fig. (i) (base side 8cm, slant height 6cm).

Surface area = Area of base + 4 × (area of one face).
Area of base = 8 × 8 = 64cm².
Area of one face = (1/2) × 8 × 6 = 24cm², so 4 faces = 96cm².
Total surface area = 64 + 96 = 160cm².

Q6. Find the total surface area of a rectangular pyramid whose area of the base is 30 square units and lateral surface area of each triangle is 25 square units.

A rectangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces.
Total lateral surface area = 4 × 25 = 100 square units.
Total surface area = Area of base + lateral surface area = 30 + 100 = 130 square units.
So the total surface area is 130 square units (the answer key writes 130cm²).

Q7. Find the volume of a rectangular pyramid whose base length and width are 10cm and 8cm and the lateral height of a triangle of base 8cm is 13cm.

The lateral height 13cm is the slant height of the face whose base is 8cm. That slant height, the vertical height h and half of the other base side (10 ÷ 2 = 5cm) form a right angled triangle.
By Pythagoras theorem: h² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so h = √144 = 12cm.
Base area = 10 × 8 = 80cm².
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height = (1/3) × 80 × 12.
Volume = 320cm³.

Q8. Given a pyramid with a square base of side 7cm. If the total surface area of the pyramid is 161cm², find its slant height.

Let the slant height be l cm. Total surface area = Area of base + 4 × (area of one face).
Area of base = 7 × 7 = 49cm².
161 = 49 + 4 × (1/2 × 7 × l).
161 − 49 = 14l, so 112 = 14l.
l = 112 ÷ 14 = 8.
So the slant height is 8cm.

Q9. Each side of a triangular based pyramid is 4cm and slant height is 8cm. Find total surface area.

Total surface area of a triangular pyramid = (1/2) × a × b + (3/2) × b × s (book), where b = 4cm is the base side, s = 8cm is the slant height and a is the altitude of the equilateral triangular base.
Altitude of the base triangle: a² = 4² − 2² = 16 − 4 = 12, so a = √12 ≈ 3.46cm.
Base area = (1/2) × 3.46 × 4 ≈ 6.93cm².
3 lateral faces = 3 × (1/2 × 4 × 8) = 48cm².
Total surface area ≈ 6.93 + 48 = 54.93cm².

Q10. The base of pyramid is a right angled triangle of sides 3cm, 4cm and 5cm. If height of pyramid is 7cm, find volume of the pyramid.

Base area = (1/2) × 3 × 4 = 6cm² (the sides 3cm and 4cm are the legs of the right angled triangle).
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height = (1/3) × 6 × 7.
Volume = 14cm³.
Note: The printed answer is 21cm², which is wrong in value and unit: the correct volume is 14cm³ (21 comes from using (1/2) instead of (1/3)).

Q11. What is the volume of a triangular pyramid whose base area is 92 inch² and height is 4 inches?

Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height.
Volume = (1/3) × 92 × 4 = 368/3 = 122⅔ inch³.
So the volume is 122⅔ cubic inches.
Note: The printed answer writes the unit as inch²; the value 122⅔ is correct but the unit of a volume must be inch³.

Q12. Find the volume of a tetrahedron whose base area is 15cm² and height is 6cm.

A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid. Volume = (1/3) × base area × height.
Volume = (1/3) × 15 × 6 = 30cm³.

Q13. Find the volume of a hexagon based pyramid with base area 23cm² and height 8cm.

Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height.
Volume = (1/3) × 23 × 8 = 184/3 = 61⅓ cm³.

Q14. The height of the Great Pyramid in Egypt is 146m and the base is a square of side 229m. Find the volume of the pyramid.

Base area = 229 × 229 = 52441m².
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height = (1/3) × 52441 × 146.
Volume = 7656386 ÷ 3 ≈ 2552128.67m³.
So the volume is about 2,552,128.67m³.
Note: The printed answer 2552.13m³ is wrong — it is about 1000 times too small; the correct volume is about 2,552,128.67m³.

Q15. The pyramid shown in Fig. (ii), has a rectangle base (10cm × 6cm). If its volume is 100cm³, find its vertical height.

Base area = 10 × 6 = 60cm².
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height, so 100 = (1/3) × 60 × h.
100 = 20 × h.
h = 100 ÷ 20 = 5.
So the vertical height is 5cm.

Q16. A pyramid with a triangular base has a volume of 50cm³. If the base and height of the triangle are 5cm and 8cm respectively, find the height of the pyramid.

Base area = (1/2) × 5 × 8 = 20cm².
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × base area × height, so 50 = (1/3) × 20 × h.
50 = (20/3) × h.
h = 50 × 3 ÷ 20 = 7.5.
So the height of the pyramid is 7.5cm.

Q17. The height and volume of a square based pyramid are 12cm and 100cm³ respectively. Find the length of the square base.

Let the side of the square base be s cm. Volume = (1/3) × base area × height.
100 = (1/3) × s² × 12.
100 = 4 × s².
s² = 100 ÷ 4 = 25, so s = √25 = 5.
So the length of the square base is 5cm.

mcqs.q: Find the total surface area of a square pyramid with base side 5cm and slant height 4cm.
mcqs.why: Base area = 5 x 5 = 25cm^2. Each face = (1/2) x 5 x 4 = 10cm^2, so 4 faces = 40cm^2. Total = 25 + 40 = 65cm^2.

mcqs.q: Find the total surface area of a square pyramid with base side 6cm and slant height 12cm.
mcqs.why: Base area = 6 x 6 = 36cm^2. Each face = (1/2) x 6 x 12 = 36cm^2, so 4 faces = 144cm^2. Total = 36 + 144 = 180cm^2.

mcqs.q: Find the total surface area of a rectangular pyramid with base 8cm x 6cm, slant height 3cm for the 8cm edges and 4cm for the 6cm edges.
mcqs.why: Base area = 8 x 6 = 48cm^2. Two faces on 8cm edges = 2 x (1/2) x 8 x 3 = 24cm^2; two on 6cm edges = 2 x (1/2) x 6 x 4 = 24cm^2. Total = 48 + 24 + 24 = 96cm^2.

mcqs.q: Find the surface area of a square pyramid of base length 12cm and slant height 15cm.
mcqs.why: Base area = 12 x 12 = 144cm^2. One face = (1/2) x 12 x 15 = 90cm^2, so 4 faces = 360cm^2. Total surface area = 144 + 360 = 504cm^2.

mcqs.q: Find the total surface area of a square pyramid with base side 10cm and slant height 6cm.
mcqs.why: Base area = 10 x 10 = 100cm^2. Each face = (1/2) x 10 x 6 = 30cm^2, so 4 faces = 120cm^2. Total = 100 + 120 = 220cm^2.

mcqs.q: A rectangular pyramid has base 10cm x 8cm and the face on the 8cm base has slant height 13cm. Find its volume.
mcqs.why: Height: h^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144, so h = 12cm (using half of the 10cm side). Base area = 80cm^2. Volume = (1/3) x 80 x 12 = 320cm^3.

mcqs.q: A square pyramid with base side 7cm has total surface area 161cm^2. Find its slant height.
mcqs.why: Base area = 7 x 7 = 49cm^2. So 161 = 49 + 4 x (1/2 x 7 x l) = 49 + 14l, giving 14l = 112 and l = 112/14 = 8cm.

mcqs.q: The base of a pyramid is a right angled triangle of sides 3cm, 4cm and 5cm, and the pyramid height is 7cm. Find its volume.
mcqs.why: Base area = (1/2) x 3 x 4 = 6cm^2, using the legs 3cm and 4cm. Volume = (1/3) x base area x height = (1/3) x 6 x 7 = 14cm^3.

mcqs.q: Find the volume of a tetrahedron whose base area is 15cm^2 and height is 6cm.
mcqs.why: A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid, so volume = (1/3) x base area x height = (1/3) x 15 x 6 = 30cm^3.

mcqs.q: The Great Pyramid has height 146m and a square base of side 229m. Find its volume.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the curved surface area of the spheres whose radii are given below (taking π ≈ 22/7): (i) r = 3.5cm (ii) r = 2.8m (iii) 0.21m

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr² (the sphere has only a curved surface). Take π ≈ 22/7.
(i) r = 3.5cm: Surface area = 4 × (22/7) × 3.5² = 4 × (22/7) × 12.25 = 154cm².
(ii) r = 2.8m: Surface area = 4 × (22/7) × 2.8² = 4 × (22/7) × 7.84 = 98.56m².
(iii) r = 0.21m: Surface area = 4 × (22/7) × 0.21² = 4 × (22/7) × 0.0441 = 0.5544m² ≈ 0.55m².

Q2. Find the radius of a sphere if its area is given by: (i) 154m² (ii) 231m² (iii) 308m²

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr². Take π ≈ 22/7, so r² = Area × 7 ÷ 88.
(i) r² = 154 × 7 ÷ 88 = 12.25, so r = √12.25 = 3.5m.
(ii) r² = 231 × 7 ÷ 88 = 18.375, so r = √18.375 ≈ 4.29m.
(iii) r² = 308 × 7 ÷ 88 = 24.5, so r = √24.5 ≈ 4.95m.

Q3. Find the volume of a sphere if r is given by: (i) 5.8cm (ii) 8.7cm (iii) 7cm (iv) 3.4m

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³. Take π ≈ 22/7.
(i) r = 5.8cm: V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 5.8³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 195.112 ≈ 817.61cm³ (answer key: 817.6cm³).
(ii) r = 8.7cm: V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 8.7³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 658.503 ≈ 2759.44cm³.
(iii) r = 7cm: V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 343 = 4312/3 ≈ 1437.33cm³.
(iv) r = 3.4m: V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 3.4³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 39.304 ≈ 164.70m³.

Q4. Find the radius and volume of each of the following spheres whose surface areas are given below: (i) 201 1/7 cm² (ii) 2.464cm² (iii) 616m²

First use Surface area = 4πr² to find r, then Volume = (4/3)πr³. Take π ≈ 22/7.
(i) 4 × (22/7) × r² = 201 1/7 = 1408/7, so r² = 1408/7 × 7/88 = 16, r = 4cm. Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 4³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 64 ≈ 268.19cm³.
(ii) 4 × (22/7) × r² = 2.464, so r² = 2.464 × 7 ÷ 88 = 0.196, r = √0.196 ≈ 0.44cm. Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 0.44³ ≈ 0.36cm³.
(iii) 4 × (22/7) × r² = 616, so r² = 616 × 7 ÷ 88 = 49, r = 7m. Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 7³ ≈ 1437.33m³.

Q5. A spherical tank is of radius 7.7m. How many litres of water can it contain?

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³. Take π ≈ 22/7.
V = (4/3) × (22/7) × 7.7³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 456.533.
V ≈ 1913.09m³.
Since 1m³ = 1000 litres, the tank can contain 1913.09 × 1000 = 1,913,090.67 litres (approx).
Note: The printed answer is 1913030.67 litres; the correct value is 1913090.67 litres (a digit slip in the printed answer).

Q6. The radius of sphere A is twice that of a sphere B. Find: (i) The ratio among their surface areas. (ii) The ratio among their volumes.

Let the radius of sphere B be r; then the radius of sphere A is 2r.
(i) Surface areas: A : B = 4π(2r)² : 4πr² = 4r² : r² = 4 : 1.
(ii) Volumes: A : B = (4/3)π(2r)³ : (4/3)πr³ = 8r³ : r³ = 8 : 1.
So the ratio of surface areas is 4:1 and the ratio of volumes is 8:1.

Q7. The surface area of a sphere is 576π cm². What will be its volume? If it is melted, how many small spheres of diameter 1cm can be made out of it?

Surface area = 4πr² = 576π, so r² = 576π ÷ 4π = 144, and r = √144 = 12cm.
Volume of the big sphere = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × π × 12³ = (4/3) × π × 1728 = 2304π cm³.
Each small sphere has diameter 1cm, so its radius is 0.5cm and its volume = (4/3) × π × 0.5³ = (4/3) × π × 0.125 = π/6 cm³.
Number of small spheres = 2304π ÷ (π/6) = 2304 × 6 = 13824.
So the volume is 2304π cm³ and 13824 small spheres can be made.

Q8. A solid copper sphere of radius 3cm is melted and electric wire of diameter 0.4cm is made out of the copper obtained. Find the length of the wire.

Volume of the sphere = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × π × 3³ = 36π cm³.
The wire is a cylinder of radius 0.4 ÷ 2 = 0.2cm. Let its length be L cm. Volume of wire = π × (0.2)² × L = 0.04π × L.
Melting keeps the volume the same: 0.04π × L = 36π.
L = 36π ÷ 0.04π = 900.
So the length of the wire is 900cm, i.e. 9m.

mcqs.q: Which formula gives the surface area of a sphere of radius r?
mcqs.why: The notes state that a sphere has only a curved surface, with surface area = 4(pi)r^2, while (4/3)(pi)r^3 is the formula for its volume.

mcqs.q: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 3.5cm (pi = 22/7).
mcqs.why: Surface area = 4 x (22/7) x 3.5^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 12.25 = 154cm^2, using surface area = 4(pi)r^2 with pi = 22/7.

mcqs.q: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 2.8m (pi = 22/7).
mcqs.why: Surface area = 4 x (22/7) x 2.8^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 7.84 = 98.56m^2, using surface area = 4(pi)r^2 with pi = 22/7.

mcqs.q: The surface area of a sphere is 154m^2. Find its radius (pi = 22/7).
mcqs.why: From 4(pi)r^2 = 154: r^2 = 154 x 7/88 = 12.25, so r = sqrt(12.25) = 3.5m, the radius of the sphere.

mcqs.q: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 7cm (pi = 22/7).
Find the volume of a sphere of radius 3cm (pi = 22/7).
mcqs.why: Volume = (4/3) x (22/7) x 3^3 = (4/3) x (22/7) x 27 = 792/7 = 113.14cm^3 approximately, and a volume is measured in cubic units.

mcqs.q: The radius of sphere A is twice the radius of sphere B. What is the ratio of their surface areas (A : B)?
mcqs.why: With radii 2r and r: surface areas are 4(pi)(2r)^2 : 4(pi)r^2 = 4r^2 : r^2, which simplifies to the ratio 4 : 1.

mcqs.q: The radius of sphere A is twice the radius of sphere B. What is the ratio of their volumes (A : B)?
mcqs.why: With radii 2r and r: volumes are (4/3)(pi)(2r)^3 : (4/3)(pi)r^3 = 8r^3 : r^3, which simplifies to the ratio 8 : 1.

mcqs.q: A solid copper sphere of radius 3cm is melted into wire of diameter 0.4cm. Find the length of the wire.
mcqs.why: Sphere volume = (4/3) x pi x 3^3 = 36pi cm^3. Wire radius = 0.2cm, so wire volume = pi x 0.2^2 x L = 0.04(pi)L. Setting 0.04(pi)L = 36pi gives L = 900cm.

mcqs.q: A sphere has surface area 576pi cm^2. If it is melted, how many small spheres of diameter 1cm can be made from it?
mcqs.why: 4(pi)r^2 = 576pi gives r^2 = 144, r = 12cm. Big volume = (4/3) x pi x 12^3 = 2304pi cm^3. Each small sphere (radius 0.5cm) has volume pi/6 cm^3, so the number is 2304pi/(pi/6) = 13824.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.5
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Calculate the surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 10cm.

Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr² (book: (1/2) × surface area of sphere + area of base = 2πr² + πr²). Take π ≈ 22/7.
Surface area = 3 × (22/7) × 10² = 3 × (22/7) × 100 = 6600/7.
Surface area ≈ 942.86cm².

Q2. The surface area of a solid hemispherical object is 150.86ft². What is the diameter of the hemisphere?

Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr². Take π ≈ 22/7.
3 × (22/7) × r² = 150.86.
r² = 150.86 × 7 ÷ 66 ≈ 16.0, so r ≈ √16 = 4ft.
Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 4 = 8ft.
So the diameter of the hemisphere is 8ft.

Q3. The surface area of a solid hemispherical object is 1356.48cm². What is the diameter of the hemisphere? (take π ≈ 3.14)

Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr² with π ≈ 3.14.
3 × 3.14 × r² = 1356.48.
r² = 1356.48 ÷ 9.42 = 144, so r = √144 = 12cm.
Diameter = 2 × 12 = 24cm.
So the diameter of the hemisphere is 24cm.

Q4. What is the total surface area of a solid hemispherical object of radius 2cm, (considering π ≈ 22/7)

Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr².
Surface area = 3 × (22/7) × 2² = 3 × (22/7) × 4 = 264/7.
Surface area ≈ 37.71cm².
Note: The printed answer is 84.86cm², which is wrong for r = 2cm: 84.86cm² is the value for r = 3cm. With the printed radius 2cm the correct area is 37.71cm².

Q5. A hemisphere has a curved surface of 175cm². Find its radius.

Curved surface area of a hemisphere = 2πr² (half of 4πr², without the flat base). Take π ≈ 22/7.
2 × (22/7) × r² = 175.
r² = 175 × 7 ÷ 44 = 1225/44 ≈ 27.84.
r = √27.84 ≈ 5.28cm (answer key: 5.276cm).
So the radius is about 5.28cm.

Q6. Find the volume of a hemisphere whose diameter is: (a) 14cm (b) 21cm (c) 10cm

Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3)πr³. Take π ≈ 22/7.
(a) Diameter 14cm, so r = 7cm: V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 7³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 343 ≈ 718.67cm³ (answer key: 718.66cm³).
(b) Diameter 21cm, so r = 10.5cm: V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 10.5³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 1157.625 = 2425.5cm³.
(c) Diameter 10cm, so r = 5cm: V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 5³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 125 ≈ 261.90cm³.
Note: The printed answer for (c) is 65.49cm³, which is wrong; with r = 5cm the correct volume is about 261.90cm³.

Q7. A hemispherical bowl has a volume of 288π cubic cm. Find the diameter of the bowl.

Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.
(2/3) × π × r³ = 288π.
r³ = 288π × 3 ÷ (2π) = 432.
r = ∛432 ≈ 7.56cm.
Diameter = 2 × 7.56 ≈ 15.12cm.
So the diameter of the bowl is about 15.12cm.

Q8. The solid shown in Fig. (i) consists of a cylinder and a hemisphere at the top. Find its volume. (Figure: total height 20cm, diameter 4cm)

Diameter = 4cm, so radius r = 2cm for both the cylinder and the hemisphere.
The hemisphere takes up r = 2cm of the total height, so height of the cylinder = 20 − 2 = 18cm.
Volume of cylinder = πr²h = 3.14 × 2² × 18 = 3.14 × 72 = 226.08cm³ (taking π ≈ 3.14, as in the answer key).
Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3) × 3.14 × 2³ = (2/3) × 3.14 × 8 ≈ 16.75cm³.
Total volume = 226.08 + 16.75 ≈ 242.83cm³.

mcqs.q: Which formula gives the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius r?
mcqs.why: The notes build it as half the sphere surface plus the base: (1/2) x 4(pi)r^2 + (pi)r^2 = 2(pi)r^2 + (pi)r^2 = 3(pi)r^2 in total.

mcqs.q: Calculate the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 10cm (pi = 22/7).
What is the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 2cm (pi = 22/7)?
mcqs.why: Total surface area = 3 x (22/7) x 2^2 = 3 x (22/7) x 4 = 264/7 = 37.714..., about 37.71cm^2 for radius 2cm.

mcqs.q: Calculate the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7cm (pi = 22/7).
mcqs.why: Total surface area = 3 x (22/7) x 7^2 = 3 x (22/7) x 49 = 3 x 154 = 462cm^2, using 3(pi)r^2 with pi = 22/7.

mcqs.q: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 150.86 square feet. What is its diameter (pi = 22/7)?
mcqs.why: 3 x (22/7) x r^2 = 150.86 gives r^2 = 150.86 x 7/66 = 16 approx, so r = 4 feet, and the diameter = 2 x 4 = 8 feet.

mcqs.q: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 1356.48cm^2. What is its diameter (pi = 3.14)?
Find the volume of a hemisphere whose diameter is 14cm (pi = 22/7).
Find the volume of a hemisphere whose diameter is 21cm (pi = 22/7).
Find the volume of a hemisphere whose diameter is 10cm (pi = 22/7).
A solid is a cylinder with a hemisphere on top; total height 20cm and diameter 4cm. Find its volume (pi = 3.14).
mcqs.why: Radius = 2cm; cylinder height = 20 - 2 = 18cm. Cylinder volume = 3.14 x 2^2 x 18 = 226.08cm^3. Hemisphere volume = (2/3) x 3.14 x 2^3 = 16.75cm^3. Total = 226.08 + 16.75 = 242.83cm^3.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.6
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Write down the missing elements of cones (all lengths are in cm). (i) r = ?, h = 8, l = 10 (ii) r = 3, h = 4, l = ? (iii) r = 9, h = ?, l = 25 (iv) Base Area = 154cm², Total Surface Area = 375cm², find r, h, l and Curved Surface Area. (Use π ≈ 22/7; l² = r² + h²; Curved Surface Area = πrl; Base Area = πr²; Total Surface Area = πr(r + l))

(i) r² = l² − h² = 10² − 8² = 100 − 64 = 36, so r = 6cm. Curved Surface Area = πrl = (22/7) × 6 × 10 ≈ 188.57cm². Base Area = πr² = (22/7) × 36 ≈ 113.14cm². Total Surface Area = 188.57 + 113.14 ≈ 301.71cm².
(ii) l² = r² + h² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25, so l = 5cm. Curved Surface Area = (22/7) × 3 × 5 ≈ 47.14cm². Base Area = (22/7) × 9 ≈ 28.29cm² (key: 28.28cm²). Total Surface Area ≈ 47.14 + 28.29 = 75.43cm² (key: 75.42cm²).
(iii) h² = l² − r² = 25² − 9² = 625 − 81 = 544, so h = √544 ≈ 23.32cm. Curved Surface Area = (22/7) × 9 × 25 ≈ 707.14cm². Base Area = (22/7) × 81 ≈ 254.57cm². Total Surface Area ≈ 707.14 + 254.57 = 961.71cm².
(iv) Base Area = πr² = 154, so r² = 154 × 7 ÷ 22 = 49 and r = 7cm. Curved Surface Area = Total Surface Area − Base Area; using the key's curved area 220cm²: l = 220 ÷ (π × 7) = 220 ÷ 22 = 10cm. Then h² = l² − r² = 100 − 49 = 51, so h = √51 ≈ 7.14cm. So r = 7cm, h ≈ 7.14cm, l = 10cm, Curved Surface Area = 220cm².
Note: In (iv) the printed Total Surface Area 375cm² is inconsistent: Base Area 154cm² + Curved Surface Area 220cm² = 374cm², so 375cm² appears to be a misprint for 374cm².

Q2. Find the volume of the cone if: (i) r = 3cm, h = 4cm (ii) r = 7cm, h = 10cm (iii) r = 5cm, l = 7cm (iv) h = 5cm, l = 8cm

Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h. Take π ≈ 22/7.
(i) V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 3² × 4 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 36 ≈ 37.71cm³ (key: 37.7cm³).
(ii) V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 7² × 10 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 490 ≈ 513.33cm³.
(iii) First find h: h² = l² − r² = 7² − 5² = 49 − 25 = 24, so h = √24 ≈ 4.90cm. V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 25 × 4.90 ≈ 128.31cm³.
(iv) First find r: r² = l² − h² = 8² − 5² = 64 − 25 = 39. V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 39 × 5 = 4290/21 ≈ 204.29cm³.
Note: The printed answers for (iii) 125.7cm³ and (iv) 201.35cm³ do not match the given data: (iii) uses h ≈ 4.8cm instead of √24 ≈ 4.90cm, giving about 128.31cm³ when computed accurately, and (iv) should be about 204.29cm³.

Q3. A conical cup is full of ice-cream. What will be the quantity of the ice-cream, if the radius and height of the cone are 4cm and 5cm respectively?

Quantity of ice-cream = Volume of the cone = (1/3)πr²h. Take π ≈ 22/7.
V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 4² × 5 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 80.
V = 1760/21 ≈ 83.81cm³ (answer key: 83.79cm³ approx).
So the cup holds about 83.8cm³ of ice-cream.

Q4. What will be the total surface area of a solid cone of height 4cm and radius 3cm?

First find the slant height: l² = r² + h² = 3² + 4² = 25, so l = 5cm.
Total Surface Area = πr(r + l) = (22/7) × 3 × (3 + 5).
Total Surface Area = (22/7) × 24 = 528/7 ≈ 75.43cm².

Q5. The area of the base of cone is 38.50cm². If its height is three times the radius of the base, find its volume.

Base Area = πr² = 38.50. Take π ≈ 22/7: r² = 38.50 × 7 ÷ 22 = 12.25, so r = √12.25 = 3.5cm.
Height h = 3 × r = 3 × 3.5 = 10.5cm.
